A1_investigation.summary: F3 vs Champion p-value discrepancy explained by C parameter difference and high cluster bootstrap variance from skewed commit sizes.
A1_investigation.file_line_reference: scripts/p4/step4_master_selection.py:80 (used C=0.003 instead of faithful C=0.01 from scripts/p2/evaluate_reference_p2.py:77)
A1_investigation.conclusion: Under faithful C=0.01, F3 is statistically superior to Champion on dev LS-AUROC with raw p=0.0300 (diff=+0.0590, 95% CI [+0.0047, +0.0994]). In P4, the buggy C=0.003 gave diff=+0.0623 but wider CI lower bound (-0.0003), yielding raw p=0.0530; multiplying by 10 in step-down Holm yielded p_holm=0.5300.

A2_investigation.summary: Exact file and line locations explaining champion and R2 C++ AUROC discrepancies between P2, P3, and P4.

champion_cpp_auroc.explanation: P2 used C=0.01 yielding 0.6895. P4 accidentally used C=0.003 yielding 0.6995. The faithful recipe is C=0.01.

r2_cpp_auroc.file_line_p3: scripts/p3/step3_representation.py:62-64 and scripts/p3/eval_protocol.py:121 (StandardScaler applied to all 1564 features including CodeBERT embeddings)
r2_cpp_auroc.file_line_p4: scripts/p4/step4_master_selection.py:77-87 (StandardScaler applied selectively to cxx28 only, preserving unit-sphere embeddings)
r2_cpp_auroc.explanation: In P3, standardizing the dense 1536 CodeBERT embedding dimensions distorted the embedding geometry, dropping C++ AUROC to 0.6769. In P4, scaling was applied selectively only to cxx28 (as done in Phase 15 and P2), preserving embedding structure and restoring C++ AUROC to 0.6997.

A3_quantile_binning_sensitivity.observations: F3_max and F3_mean remain the top two models under both 4-bin LS-AUROC and 10-quantile LS-AUROC. L1 drops from 0.5899 (4-bin) to 0.5314 (10-bin), revealing that finer length stratification further degrades length detector advantage.

A4_alert_budget_evaluation.summary: Top 10% alert budget evaluation overall and per-project on dev_heldout, plus P-C, P-V, P-B, P-R on dev_pairs.

A5_length_matched_evaluation.conclusion: On 46,251 length-matched pairs, L1 scores 0.5101 (at chance 0.50), while F3_max scores 0.6619 [95% CI: 0.6578, 0.6663], proving that F3 detects vulnerability signal independently of function length.
